editorial:
Twenty-nine years after the Sanderson sisters first terrorized Salem, the Black Flame Candle is lit again, bringing Winifred, Sarah, and Mary back for another night of chaos. This time, three high school friends—Becca, Izzy, and Cassie—find themselves caught in the middle of the witches' plan to get revenge and gain ultimate power. The movie keeps the same silly, spooky energy as the original, with plenty of laughs, musical moments, and Halloween spirit. It feels like a warm reunion with old friends, especially if you grew up watching the first film. The story moves quickly and never takes itself too seriously, making it an easy watch on a cozy October night.

The three leads bring fresh energy, and Bette Midler, Sarah Jessica Parker, and Kathy Najimy slip back into their roles like no time has passed. The musical numbers are fun, and the costumes and sets look great. On the downside, the plot can feel a bit rushed, and some jokes land better than others. Still, if you want a light, family-friendly Halloween movie, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final act, the Sanderson sisters try to cast a spell that will make them all-powerful, but it requires a sacrifice. Winifred's sisters turn to dust when the spell backfires, and Winifred refuses to let them go, choosing to join them instead. The girls use their own magic to stop the spell and save Salem. In the end, the witches are gone, and the three friends celebrate Halloween together, having grown closer through the adventure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves nostalgic Halloween comedies and family-friendly fantasy.
